To determine whether the proposed solution is correct, we analyze the definition of Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information and its high-SNR asymptotic behavior.

Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information of order $\alpha > 0, \alpha \neq 1$ between $X$ and $Y$ is defined as:
$$I_\alpha(X; Y) = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 1} \log \int \left( \sum_x P_X(x) p_{Y|X}(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} dy$$

Given the model $Y = \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} X + Z$ with $Z \sim \mathcal{N}(0, 1)$, the conditional density is:
$$p_{Y|X}(y|x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}} \exp\left( -\frac{(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$
Thus,
$$p_{Y|X}(y|x)^\alpha = (2\pi)^{-\alpha/2} \exp\left( -\frac{\alpha(y - \sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x)^2}{2} \right)$$

As $\mathsf{snr} \to \infty$, the support points $\sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x_i$ become well-separated. In the neighborhood of $\sqrt{\mathsf{snr}} x_i$, the $i$-th term in the mixture dominates:
$$\left( \sum_j P(x_j) p_{Y|X}(y|x_j)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} \approx P(x_i)^{1/\alpha} p_{Y|X}(y|x_i)$$
Integrating over the real line yields:
$$\int \left( \sum_x P(x) p_{Y|X}(y|x)^\alpha \right)^{1/\alpha} dy \xrightarrow{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha}$$

Substituting this into Sibson's $\alpha$-mutual information gives:
$$\lim_{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} I_\alpha(X; Y) = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 1} \log \sum_x P(x)^{1/\alpha}$$

Recall the definition of the Rényi entropy of order $\beta$:
$$H_\beta(X) = \frac{1}{1 - \beta} \log \sum_x P(x)^\beta$$

Setting $\beta = \frac{1}{\alpha}$:
$$\frac{1}{1 - \beta} = \frac{1}{1 - 1/\alpha} = \frac{\alpha}{\alpha - 1}$$
which matches the prefactor and the power inside the sum, giving:
$$\lim_{\mathsf{snr} \to \infty} I_\alpha(X; Y) = H_{1/\alpha}(X)$$

Therefore, the correct order is $\beta = \frac{1}{\alpha}$, not $\beta = \frac{1}{1-\alpha}$ (which would also become negative for $\alpha > 1$, violating the definition of Rényi entropy).

VERDICT: REJECT
